knowledge:
- key_parameters: data=The input dataframe, matrix, or SummarizedExperiment to adjust. Must contain at least two samples per batch and 2 features ;; cores=Number of cores for parallelization via BiocParallel. Default is NULL (uses BiocParallel::bpparam()) ;; combatmode=Integer (1 to 4) encoding ComBat parameters (par.prior and mean.only). Ignored if method is not "ComBat" ;; corereduction=Positive integer indicating the factor by which the number of processes should be reduced when no further adjustment is possible for the current number of batches ;; stopParBatches=Positive integer indicating the minimum number of batches required at a hierarchy level to proceed with parallelized adjustment ;; backend=The backend to use for inter-process communication ('default' or 'file') ;; method=The underlying batch effect correction method ('ComBat', 'limma', or 'ref') ;; qualitycontrol=A boolean to (de)activate the ASW (average silhouette score) computation ;; verify=A boolean to (de)activate the initial format check of the input data ;; labelname=A string containing the name of the column to use as class labels (default "Label") ;; batchname=A string containing the name of the column to use as batch labels (default "Batch") ;; referencename=A string containing the name of the column to use as reference labels (default "Reference") ;; covariatename=A vector containing the names of columns with categorical covariables (default NULL) ;; BPPARAM=An instance of BiocParallelParam to be used for parallelization ;; assayname=The name of the assay to apply BERT to if the input is a SummarizedExperiment object
- alternatives: HarmonizR is a Bioconductor package addressing similar data integration challenges, but BERT provides better execution time, better data coverage, a more user-friendly design, and a less error-prone input format.
- when_to_use: Use BERT when you need to perform batch-effect correction on high-dimensional omics datasets (especially proteomics) that contain missing values (NAs) and require fast, parallelized processing across multiple batches.
- pitfalls: Each batch must contain at least two samples ;; Missing values (NA) are not allowed in Label, Cov_x, or Reference columns ;; BERT requires at least two numeric values per batch and unique covariate level to adjust a feature, otherwise the feature is set to NA for that batch ;; Reference-based adjustment requires at least two references of common class per adjustment step ;; The Reference column is mutually exclusive with covariate columns.

workflows.name: standard_batch_correction
workflows.intent: Perform batch-effect correction on a data frame or matrix using ComBat or limma, with optional parallel processing.
input: expression_data.csv (A tabular file with samples in rows, features in columns, and a mandatory 'Batch' column indicating batch membership)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the expression data ;; 2. Run BERT batch correction specifying the method (ComBat or limma) and parallelization cores
workflows.code:
library(BERT)
# generate test data with 10% missing values as provided by the BERT library
dataset_raw <- generate_dataset(features=60, batches=10, samplesperbatch=10, mvstmt=0.1, classes=2)
# apply BERT
dataset_adjusted <- BERT(dataset_raw)

# Alternative: Sequential adjustment with limma
dataset_adjusted <- BERT(dataset_raw, method="limma")

# Alternative: Parallel batch effect correction with ComBat
dataset_adjusted <- BERT(dataset_raw, cores=2)

workflows.name: summarized_experiment_correction
workflows.intent: Perform batch-effect correction directly on a SummarizedExperiment object.
input: summarized_experiment.rds (A SummarizedExperiment object containing an assay matrix and colData with Batch metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the SummarizedExperiment object ;; 2. Run BERT batch correction by specifying the target assay name
workflows.code:
nrows <- 200
ncols <- 8
# SummarizedExperiments store samples in columns and features in rows (in contrast to BERT).
# BERT will automatically account for this.
expr_values <- matrix(runif(nrows * ncols, 1, 1e4), nrows)
# colData also takes further metadata information, such as Label, Sample,
# Reference or Covariables
colData <- data.frame("Batch"=c(1,1,1,1,2,2,2,2), "Label"=c(1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2), "Sample"=c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8))
dataset_raw = SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(assays=list(expr=expr_values), colData=colData)
dataset_adjusted = BERT(dataset_raw, assayname = "expr")

workflows.name: covariate_batch_correction
workflows.intent: Perform batch-effect correction while preserving biological variation of interest by specifying categorical covariates.
input: expression_data_with_covariates.csv (A tabular file containing expression values, a 'Batch' column, and one or more covariate columns prefixed with 'Cov_')
workflows.stages: 1. Load the expression data containing covariate columns ;; 2. Run BERT batch correction (covariates are automatically detected or specified via covariatename)
workflows.code:
# import BERT
library(BERT)
# set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(1)
# generate data with 5 batches, 60 features, 30 samples per batch, 15% missing values and 2 classes
dataset_raw <- generate_dataset(features=60, batches=5, samplesperbatch=30, mvstmt=0.15, classes=2)
# create covariable column with 2 possible values, e.g. male/female condition
dataset_raw["Cov_1"] = sample(c(1,2), size=dim(dataset_raw)[1], replace=TRUE)
# BERT
dataset_adjusted <- BERT(dataset_raw)

workflows.name: reference_based_correction
workflows.intent: Perform batch-effect correction using reference samples (bridges) when class distributions are severely skewed across batches.
input: expression_data_with_references.csv (A tabular file containing expression values, a 'Batch' column, and a 'Reference' column indicating reference classes or 0 for co-adjusted samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the expression data containing the Reference column ;; 2. Run BERT batch correction with method set to "ref"
workflows.code:
# import BERT
library(BERT)
# generate data with 4 batches, 6 features, 15 samples per batch, 15% missing values and 2 classes
dataset_raw <- generate_dataset(features=6, batches=4, samplesperbatch=15, mvstmt=0.15, classes=2)
# create reference column with default value 0.  The 0 indicates, that the respective sample should be co-adjusted only.
dataset_raw[, "Reference"] <- 0
# randomly select 2 references per batch and class - in practice, this choice will be determined by external requirements (e.g. class known for only these samples)
batches <- unique(dataset_raw$Batch) # all the batches
for(b in batches){ # iterate over all batches
    # references from class 1
    ref_idx = sample(which((dataset_raw$Batch==b)&(dataset_raw$Label==1)), size=2, replace=FALSE)
    dataset_raw[ref_idx, "Reference"] <- 1
    # references from class 2
    ref_idx = sample(which((dataset_raw$Batch==b)&(dataset_raw$Label==2)), size=2, replace=FALSE)
    dataset_raw[ref_idx, "Reference"] <- 2
}
# BERT
dataset_adjusted <- BERT(dataset_raw, method="ref")
